title: Decision-making political institutions (1–2)

paras.en: Which are the decision-making political institutions?
paras.ur: فیصلہ ساز سیاسی ادارے کون سے ہیں؟ (Decision Making Political Institutions)
paras.ps: پرېکړه کوونکې سیاسي ادارې کومې دي؟ (Decision Making Political Institutions)

paras.en: The institutions that seek lasting solutions and make durable policy for running the affairs of the country and solving important problems are called political decision-making. In ancient times, because of the simplicity of the political system, the chief of a tribe used to make decisions after consulting a few companions; in the same way a king would consult courtiers but kept the power of decision-making with himself. In the present age, however, in any democratic system many institutions are engaged in decision-making activities, among them the common people along with the elite. In political decision-making different institutions of the country play their roles in different parts.
paras.ur: ملکی امور چلانے اور اہم مسائل حل کرنے کے لیے ادارے جو دیرپا حل تلاش کرتے ہیں اور پائیدار پالیسی بناتے ہیں اس کو سیاسی فیصلہ سازی کہا جاتا ہے۔ قدیم دور میں سیاسی نظام کی سادگی کی وجہ سے قبیلے کا سردار چند ساتھیوں کی مشاورت سے فیصلہ سازی کیا کرتا تھا اسی طرح بادشاہ درباریوں سے مشورہ کرتا تھا لیکن فیصلہ سازی کا اختیار اپنے پاس رکھتا تھا لیکن دورِ حاضر میں کسی بھی جمہوری نظام میں کئی ادارے فیصلہ سازی کی سرگرمیوں میں مصروف ہوتے ہیں جن میں خواص کے ساتھ عوام بھی شامل ہیں۔ سیاسی فیصلہ سازی میں ملک کے مختلف ادارے مختلف حصوں میں اپنا کردار ادا کرتے ہیں۔

paras.en: In any country the real responsibility for administration lies with the political executive or administration. The political administration is the elected executive of the country. In a democratic system the president, king or queen, prime minister, ministers, governors, advisers, provincial chief ministers and provincial ministers and so on are collectively called the political executive or administration, and their role in political decision-making is the most important. The central and provincial cabinets make decisions after mutual consultation. In a presidential system the president has the important power of decision-making; for example, in America the president has great importance. In a parliamentary system the prime minister and cabinet have the power of decision-making, as in Pakistan, India, Britain and so on.
